Luray Caverns Motels
Enjoy a quiet setting at the East building, designed with accents of native stone and located just opposite the Luray Singing Tower. Or relax in the one-story, colonial-style West building. Both locations are set against the stunning backdrop of Shenandoah National Park, with beautiful views of the Blue Ridge Mountains. And both are located just moments away from Luray Caverns.

Mimslyn Inn
Be transported to the antebellum era of the Old South at Luray’s iconic Mimslyn Inn, a member of Historic Hotels of America. Enjoy meals at the elegant Circa ’31, or the laid-back Speakeasy Tavern. The Cottage Collection and Manor House offer the perfect atmosphere for romantic getaways, bridal parties, golf outings and family gatherings of all kinds.
Book Now
Skyland
Located in Shenandoah National Park at the highest elevation along Skyline Drive, Skyland offers breathtaking views of the Shenandoah Valley. Enjoy a farm-to-fork meal in the Pollock Dining Room, or stop in the Mountain Taproom for a lighter fare. Take a horseback ride from Skyland stables and enjoy free nightly entertainment for the whole family. The historic conference building is the perfect setting for weddings and group events.
Book Now
Enjoy two peaceful nights at Skyland with the Clifftops Caverns Package , and experience spring in the Blue Ridge at its most serene. Wake up above the clouds. Breathe in fresh mountain air. Watch golden sunsets stretch across the ridgeline. Then explore the awe-inspiring beauty of Luray Caverns. Click below for details and to book your getaway.
Clifftops Caverns Package
Big Meadows Lodge
Built with stones cut from the Massanutten Mountains and wood from the area’s native chestnut trees, the Lodge – listed on the National Register of Historic Places – is the ideal place to relax and unwind. After exploring the surrounding Shenandoah National Park, experience a variety of seasonal dishes, local wines and family entertainment.
Book Now
Shawnee Farms Estate
Discover the solitude of old Virginia at Shawnee Farm in this elegant, historic farm home with exquisite views of the Shenandoah Valley. Originally built in 1863, the home was recently renovated, can accommodate up to 16 guests, and is just two miles from Luray. Amenities include a kitchen with modern appliances, a large formal dining area, lounging room and large parlor room, six pristine bathrooms, multiple screened in porches upstairs and downstairs, a large entertainment room, modern washer and dryer, and more.
For more information on Shawnee Farms Estate, call us directly at (540) 743-6551 option #4 or visit  shawneefarmsestate.com

pages.text:
Our Story - Luray Caverns
Our Story
Our History
It all started on August 13, 1878…
…when Andrew Campbell, William Campbell, and Benton Stebbins were walking in a field and felt a rush of cold air coming from a limestone sinkhole which was unusual on a hot summer day. And so, the discovery was on! Andrew, three other men, and his 13-year-old nephew, Quint, began exploring the area searching for a cave. They dug away loose rocks and sticks for four hours before Andrew and Quint slid down by a rope into the cave with candles in hand. When they got down there, they could hardly believe their eyes. The men had just discovered Luray Caverns, the largest series of caverns in Eastern America.
See the Stalac-Timeline
Luray Caverns History Timeline
4 Million Centuries in the Making
May 7, 2023
2023
1st Discovery Tour
January 1, 2020
2020
Shawnee Farms Estate hosted its first wedding.
May 7, 2019
2019
New Entrance to Luray Caverns
January 1, 2019
2019
Shawnee Farms Estate opened for lodging.
January 1, 2015
2015
The Caverns began offering souvenir photos.
January 1, 2013
2013
Heartpine Café joined the Shenandoah Heritage Village. The two-bay log “Switzer” barn was originally built by Israel Burner on his Shenandoah River farm.
January 1, 2012
2012
The Rope Adventure Park was added. This two-level rope course challenge offers unending opportunities for self-discovery and growth.
January 1, 2009
2009
Shenandoah Heritage Village is a presentation of 19th-century structures, from the 1750 to the 1920s. The Main Museum is named the Luray Valley Museum. Around this museum are other smaller buildings that have been transported to the site and restored to represent a small 19th century farming community.
January 1, 1998
1998
The Garden Maze was created by John Schneider. It is separately owned and rented from Luray Caverns. The Maze is the largest garden maze in the mid-Atlantic.
January 1, 1977
1977
The Luray Fudge Company was started by Jim Garrahy. Erik Atkins took ownership in 2000.
January 1, 1976
1976
Designed by Mal Purdy of Livingston, New Jersey, Caverns Country Club Resort opened in May 1976 by the Luray Caverns Corporation. It covers 6,499 yards with an 18-hole, par 72 course. The first hole has a nearby small sink hole and there was no penalty if a golf ball went in there.
January 1, 1974
1974
Luray Caverns was designated a Registered Natural National Landmark.
January 1, 1967
1967
Tower Motels, now known as Luray Caverns East Motels, were built. They were previously owned by Cletus Presgraves, moved from the foot of New Market Mountain, and were restored in the late 1960s.
January 1, 1957
1957
The Car and Carriage Caravan Museum was opened, housing, 140 items related to transportation, including fully restored cars, carriages, and coaches dating from as early as 1727. Prizes in the collection of restored authentic vehicles include an 1898 Benz and the oldest car in operating condition in the country.
The Wishing Well was started after management noticed visitors throwing coins into various pools of water throughout the caverns and decided to dedicate one place along the tour for them to do so
The West Motel was built in 1954 and was originally owned and operated by Mr. Augustus M. Modisett.
January 1, 1954
1954
The Great Stalacpipe Organ was invented by Leland W. Sprinkle of Springfield, Virginia. Mr. Sprinkle was inspired as he was taking a tour and watched as a tour guide tapped on a formation with a mallet. The organ was dedicated in 1957.
May 7, 1950
1950 s
The cave in the 1950 s
January 1, 1950
1950
Paved walkways were constructed. They replaced wooden planks that were used as pathways.
January 1, 1937
1937
The Luray Carillon Singing Tower was built in memory of T.C. Northcott’s wife, Belle Northcott. It is 117 feet tall and contains a carillon of 47 bells. The largest bell weighs 7,640 pounds and is six feet in diameter. The smallest bell weighs 12 ½ pounds. It is recognized as one of the country’s major carillons where regularly scheduled recitals are held, free-of-charge through the spring, summer, and fall.
January 1, 1905
1905
The Luray Caverns Corporation, created by T.C. Northcott, purchased the cavern s property.
January 1, 1901
1901
T.C. Northcott purchased Luray Caverns and built a sanatorium house (a specialized house made to treat specific ailments) named “Limair” for his wife, Belle, who had a respiratory illness. “Limair” became the first air-conditioned building in America by connecting a shaft to the Caverns that allowed the naturally purified underground air to fill every room.
January 1, 1893
1893
J. Kemp Barlett of Baltimore and T.C. Northcott of Emira, New York, leased the cave from The Luray Caverns Company until 1901.
October 1, 1890
1890
David Kagery of Luray, and George Marshall of Uniontown, Pennsylvania, purchased the property. In October, The Valley Land and Improvement Company bought the Caverns.
January 1, 1881
1881
Sam Buracker owned the land but it was up for sale at the time of the discovery to pay for his delinquent taxes. The Campbells bought the land without telling Mr. Buracker of their findings until after they had purchased it.
The Virginia Supreme Court ruled against the Campbells and the land was given back to Mr. Buracker’s creditor, Mr. William T. Biedler, who was also his son-in-law. Once Mr. Buracker’s family got the land back, Mr. Biedler sold the property to the Luray Cave and Hotel Company.
Thirteen arc lights were installed in the cave and powered by an engine-driven generator near the train station, seven miles away. In the United States, this was the first instance on record that the cave was lighted by electricity.
August 13, 1878
1878
Luray Caverns was discovered on August 13 by Andrew Campbell, William Campbell, and Benton Stebbins. As they walked through a field, they began to move rocks and sticks anywhere they felt cool air coming up from the ground.
May 7, 1878
1878
Andrew Campbell at the discovery point

pages.text:
Frequently Asked Questions - Luray Caverns
Plan Your Visit
Frequently Asked Questions
General Admission $36
$34 for seniors | $18 for children 6-12 | FREE under age 6
Includes the Luray Caverns Self-Guided Tour, the Car Carriage Caravan Museum, Shenandoah Heritage Village, and Toy Town Junction
Buy Tickets
Group Rates Available
Tours Pricing
Do I need reservations to tour Luray Caverns?
You don’t need a reservation to tour the Caverns. Many guests purchase tickets upon arrival.
What if I miss my timed ticket entry?
We never sell out, and you can always gain access to the Caverns during operating hours.
How long does it take to tour Luray Caverns?
A self-guided tour of the Caverns takes a little over an hour. However, we recommend allowing 2-3 hours to tour the Caverns and experience the other attractions included with your general admission ticket.
What is included in the admission cost?
General Admission includes Luray Caverns, the Car & Carriage Caravan Museum, Toy Town Junction, and the Shenandoah Heritage Village.
Are there any discounts for individuals?
There are several ways you can get discounts on your entrance to Luray Caverns.
Children 5 and under: no charge when accompanied by a parent or guardian.
Groups of 20 or more receive discounted admission.
$11.00 student tickets (through grade 12) for school-sponsored educational groups with 15 students or more.
50% off your second adult ticket with a Giant or Martin’s BonusCard.
$6 off admission from participating military bases or discount tickets through participating MWR/ITT offices.
Do you have group rates?
Groups of 20 or more receive discounts. We ask that large groups contact our Reservation Office, 540-743-6551, a couple of weeks before their planned arrival.
How much do the Guided Discovery Tours cost?
Adult $65
Children $35
No discounts will be applied to Discovery Tour admission cost.
Directions, Parking Hours
What is the GPS address for Luray Caverns?
101 Cave Hill Rd, Luray, VA 22835
When are you open for tours?
Luray Caverns is open every day of the year. Self-guided tours depart after 9 am.
From April 1 to June 14
Daily 9am – 6pm
From June 15 to Labor Day
Daily 9am – 7pm
After Labor Day to October 31
Daily 9am – 6pm
From November 1 to March 31
Weekdays 9am – 4pm
Weekends 9am – 5pm
Where can I park and is parking free?
There’s a free lot and plenty of open spaces near the entrance. Follow the signs from the driveway.
I drive a large RV, should I park in the regular lot?
Yes, we have ample free parking for RVs. If you plan on visiting during a holiday or holiday weekend, please call us in advance to confirm availability.
Do you close during bad weather events?
Outside weather does not affect tours of the cavern. We’re open every day of the year, rain or shine.
Inside Luray Caverns
Can I take photos in the Caverns?
You’re more than welcome to take photos. Remember to tag us  @luraycaverns if you share them on Instagram.
Is it cold in the Caverns? / What should I wear in Luray Caverns?
The Caverns are a constant 54°F with very high humidity, which makes it feel more like 65°F. Some people prefer to bring a light jacket while touring the Caverns. We also recommend wearing comfortable walking shoes.
Can I play the Great Stalacpipe Organ?
No. Performances from the console are only approved for publicity purposes involving television programs, news segments, documentaries, or celebrity appearances.
Are food and drink allowed inside Luray Caverns?
Food and drink are not allowed in the Caverns. We have snack and dining options available near our Welcome Center. However, it is okay to bring a picnic on the grounds.
Can I bring my pet?
Leashed pets are allowed on the Luray Caverns grounds outside. Guests are permitted to carry small pets on the tour.
Accessibility
Is there wheelchair and mobility scooter access?
Our  step-free entrance will accommodate wheelchairs; however, Luray Caverns is not listed as handicapped accessible. The paved walkways on the tour are 1.25 miles in length with some areas having moderate grades that may require assistance for visitors with disabilities.
Are strollers allowed inside Luray Caverns?
Paved walkways are not usually too steep for strollers. We recommend bringing a small stroller.
Is it dark inside the Caverns? Will I need a flashlight?
You don’t need a flashlight. We are proud to offer tours along well-lighted, paved walkways throughout the Caverns.
Are there any areas of the Caverns that may be challenging for individuals with mobility challenges?
Some areas of the 1.25-mile path have moderate grades that may require assistance for visitors with disabilities.
Are there designated accessible parking spaces available close to the entrance of Luray Caverns?
Yes.
Are there restrooms in the Caverns?
No, there are no restrooms inside Luray Caverns. Please use the facilities above ground before entering for the Caverns tour.
Weddings and Events
Do you hold weddings inside Luray Caverns?
Yes, we hold weddings after our regular business hours . Visit our Weddings & Groups page to learn more.
Do you have wedding packages available?
We have three packages available to have your dream wedding at Luray Caverns:
Luray Caverns Private Ceremony
Rate: $3,000
Designed for small, intimate weddings with up to 12 guests
Luray Caverns Cathedral Wedding Package
Rate: $9,000
Designed for large weddings with up to 100 guests
Luray Caverns Ceremony & Shawnee Farms Estate Reception & Lodging
Rate: $12,000
Designed for large weddings with up to 100 guests
2 Nights Lodging included in this package
For more details about the three packages, please visit our Weddings & Groups  page.
Do you have any venues for special events?
Yes. Burner Barn is available to host special events such as:
Rehearsal Dinners
Corporate Events
Birthday Celebrations
To learn more or request information about Burner Barn, please visit our Weddings & Events page.
Do you have engagement or elopement packages?
Yes. Our Luray Caverns Proposal Package i

Shenandoah Heritage Village - Luray Caverns
Explore
Shenandoah Heritage Village
General Admission $36
$34 for seniors | $18 for children 6-12 | FREE under age 6
Includes the Luray Caverns Self-Guided Tour, the Car Carriage Caravan Museum, Shenandoah Heritage Village, and Toy Town Junction
Buy Tickets
Group Rates Available
An Adventure Through Time
Discover the rich history of the Shenandoah Valley at the Shenandoah Heritage Village.
The Shenandoah Heritage Village is a seven-acre re-creation of a small 19th century farming community made up of restored historic buildings, cottage style gardens, and a small vineyard with a scenic mountain backdrop.
Admission
Visit Shenandoah Heritage Village FREE with Luray Caverns general admission.
Historical buildings and grounds are open every day to the public from 10a until dusk, weather permitting.
See Collection Website
Structures
Some were moved here whole; others were rebuilt brick by brick.
These endangered historic buildings were given a new life, through relocation and restoration, to help whisk you away to Shenandoah living in the 19th century.
The Elk Run Dunkard Meeting House
Collections
The Luray Valley Museum is home to quite the collection .
Ranging from pre-contact Native American history to the Roaring 20s, you’ll be amazed at just how rich the history of the Shenandoah Valley is.
Spitler Blanket Chest
Gardens and Vineyard
As you stroll along the paths of the Shenandoah Heritage Village, you’ll notice gardens full of rare heirloom plants, fruit trees, and a small vineyard. Nigella, wallflowers, foxgloves, and sunflowers are just some of the blooms that await.
Willy House summer garden
Gem Mining Sluice
Get a hands-on history lesson that’s fun for the whole family.
The Stonyman Mining Company Gem Sluice is an interactive lesson in how pioneer prospectors would bring gold and other valuable gems into the world. Gem bags can be purchased in the Museum Gift Shop.
Learn More About the Mining Sluice
Stonyman Mining Company Gem Sluice
Heartpine Café
Under the Burner Barn you’ll find a recharging station. For humans.
Along with delicious lunches and refreshing drinks, the Heartpine Café also offers regional wines, beer, and hard ciders that all pair nicely with the beautiful views.
The Heartpine Café
Museum Gift Shop
Whether it’s for you or someone else, our gift shop has a wide range of books, handmade pottery, and other keepsakes that make an already incredible trip truly unforgettable.
The Museum Gift Shop
